p1.title: Traceability Gate Produces False PASS — Two Plans Silently Skip
p1.description: The enforcer's default mode selects only the latest-mtime requirements.md (currently self-judging-workflow). Running the CLAUDE.md-mandated gate shows PASS while dev-workflow-platform (34 unimplemented FRs) and dependency-linking (7 stale FRs) silently fail. Any agent running the gate believes traceability is clean when it is not.
p1.exploit_scenario: Any pipeline agent runs `python3 tools/traceability-enforcer.py`, sees PASS, and proceeds to merge code with completely unimplemented feature requirements — silent drift accumulates
p1.impact: Architecture rule 'Every FR needs a test' is unenforceable at scale; spec-first discipline breaks down
p1.recommendation: Run gate explicitly against all plans: `python3 tools/traceability-enforcer.py --all` or enumerate plans in CLAUDE.md. Add --all flag to enforcer script.

p1.title: FR-001 through FR-032: dev-workflow-platform Entirely Unimplemented
p1.description: The dev-workflow-platform spec (69 FRs: feature requests, bug reports, dev cycles, SQLite backend, full React UI) was approved in plan run-1774234977 but never dispatched to a coder team. Current Source/ implements a completely different domain (self-judging workflow engine). Git history has only one commit.
p1.exploit_scenario: Stakeholders believe the platform is spec-compliant; 34 committed FRs have zero implementation and zero tests
p1.impact: Entire product domain is misaligned with specifications; cannot pass traceability audit
p1.recommendation: Decision required: (a) Archive spec as superseded — move to Specifications/archived/ and close the plan, or (b) Dispatch TheATeam to implement. Must resolve before next audit.

p2.title: Stale FR IDs in dependency-linking Plan
p2.description: FR IDs (FR-0002, FR-0003, FR-070, FR-085, etc.) reference a portal/ codebase that no longer exists in Source/. The feature was implemented under FR-dependency-* IDs. Requirements file was never updated after implementation.
p2.recommendation: Update requirements.md to use the actual FR IDs implemented, or mark plan as archived.

p2.title: Silent Error Swallowing on Non-2xx JSON Parse
p2.description: .catch(() => ({})) silently swallows JSON parse errors on non-2xx responses (e.g., HTML 502 from a proxy). The caller receives an empty object instead of an error, masking real failures.
p2.exploit_scenario: Backend returns 502 HTML error page; frontend silently treats it as empty JSON — no error displayed to user, state corrupted
p2.impact: Violates 'never swallow errors silently' architecture rule; masks production errors from operators
p2.recommendation: Add rationale comment or log at debug level: `.catch(err => { logger.debug('json parse failed', err); return {}; })`
